summary: Plays video from a URL or MediaStream, with play/pause/restart/reset signals and playback-position output.
description: Video renders an HTML `video` element. `src` (a string URL or project asset path) or `srcObject` (a MediaStream, e.g. a camera feed) supplies the media; `poster` shows an image before playback; `autoplay`, `loop`, `muted`, `controls` and `volume` map directly onto the element. Playback is driven by four signal inputs: `play` resumes, `pause` pauses, `restart` seeks to the start and plays, `reset` seeks to the start and pauses. Outputs report state: `onPlay`/`onPause`/`onCanPlay` are signals from the element's events, `onTimeUpdate` (Playback Position) is a number holding the current time in seconds, and `videoWidth`/`videoHeight` give the intrinsic size once known.
whenToUse: Embedded video content, background/hero loops, and camera previews (wire a media stream to `srcObject`). For still pictures use Image. Browsers block unmuted autoplay — combine `autoplay` with `muted` for background video, or start playback from a user action via `play`.

ports.src: String value: URL or project asset path of the video file.
ports.srcObject: MediaStream value; when set, the element plays the stream instead of `src` — used for camera/microphone previews.
ports.play: Signal; resumes playback of the current source.
ports.restart: Signal; seeks to time 0 and plays.
ports.reset: Signal; seeks to time 0 and pauses — 'stop'.
ports.onTimeUpdate: Number value (Playback Position): current playback time in seconds, updated as the video plays.
ports.onCanPlay: Signal; fires when enough data is buffered to start playing — a good moment to reveal the player.
ports.onVideoElementCreated: DOM-element reference to the underlying `video` element, for custom JavaScript integration.

runtimeBehavior: Declared-port-groups: `width`/`height` appear based on `sizeMode`, per-side border width/color ports appear once a border style is chosen, and `pointerEventsEnabled` appears when `pointerEventsMode` is 'explicit'. The playback and event ports are always present.
patterns: Button `onClick` → `play`: user-initiated playback that satisfies browser autoplay policies.
antiPatterns: Expecting `autoplay` alone to start sound-on playback — browsers refuse; either set `muted` or trigger `play` from a user gesture.
